name: The Oriental Plane of the Abraham Dolehof

location.address: Abraham Dolehof, Utrecht (enter via the gate on Lange Nieuwstraat)

verified_sources: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen v2024 (Bomenstichting), entry nr 1688792, data/registers/netherlands-lrmb.json
https://www.duic.nl/cultuur/geheimen-van-de-stad-de-plataan-de-dolehof/ (DUIC, 2018-07-15, reporting a Gilde Utrecht guided-tour text)
access: Free, but daytime only: the courtyard gate on Lange Nieuwstraat is closed in the evening. The residents who live around the garden maintain it.
transport: About a 12-15 minute walk from Utrecht Centraal station
verify_notes: Alive: register status 3 (not the dead/felled status 5 code seen elsewhere in this register), owner_category gemeente, visitable 'ja'. Two sources agree closely on planting era: LRMB register band 1840-1850 (176-186 years as of 2026); DUIC's 2018 article independently states the tree was 'approximately 170 years old' at that time, implying planting around 1848, which sits inside the register's band. No bridge claim needed, the two sources converge on their own. Girth reported as 'more than four metres' (over 400cm) at breast height, DUIC 2018; recorded girth_cm 400 as a floor, not a precise figure. Height reported as about 25 metres. Species: Oriental Plane (Platanus orientalis), stated explicitly by both the register and DUIC; not a London Plane hybrid. Setting/story material: stands in the Abraham Dolehof, a small walled former convent garden (Sint-Ursula nunnery, founded 1412 by Abraham Dole and his wife Christina, dissolved 1580) tucked between the Oudegracht, Hamburgerstraat and Lange Nieuwstraat. Freely open to the public during the day via the Lange Nieuwstraat gate, closed at night; residents around the courtyard maintain the garden. The Lutheran church, a former clandestine church built to look like an ordinary house after the Reformation, is visible from the garden. The register's own history text for this entry closely mirrors the DUIC article's wording (both trace to a Gilde Utrecht guided-tour text), so treat them as one strand of provenance corroborated by an official register plus a dated news publication, rather than two fully independent narratives; the register's designation itself is the second, separately-maintained source. Trunk described as covered in harmless 'warts' (burrs) and peeling bark in a brown-green mottled pattern; leaves deeply incised; seed balls in clusters of three to six. monumentaltrees.com also lists this exact tree at this address (title match in search results) as a further, uncontacted cross-check; its page itself 403'd to curl this pass and was not read directly, so no figures from it are used here. Collectible point: yes, one identifiable specimen, the garden's only mature tree of note. Visible='nee' in the register only means it cannot be seen from outside the gate, not that entry is restricted.

name: The Gnarled Plane of the Tolsteegbrug
verified_sources: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen v2024 (Bomenstichting), entry nr 1688688, data/registers/netherlands-lrmb.json
https://kanokaartutrecht.nl/monumentalebomen.html (stop 5 of the canal-side monumental trees route, photos dated through January 2026)
access: Free, in the public Manenburg park beside the Tolsteegbrug bridge
transport: About a 15-20 minute walk south from Utrecht Centraal station, or a short bus ride to Tolsteegsingel
verify_notes: Alive: register status 3, owner_category gemeente, visitable 'ja'. Corroborated and dated recently: kanokaartutrecht.nl's canal-side monumental-trees walking route (an independently maintained hobby site, already used by an earlier pass for other Utrecht trees, see leads.json) lists this exact register number (1688688) as stop 5 of its route, with a photo dated as recently as 5 January 2026, which is strong evidence of current life. Age: the register's own history field for this specific tree gives a municipal planting record of 1835 ('Plantjaar volgens gemeente: 1835'), which is a documented planting date for this specimen rather than a garden-wide guess, so it is a firmer basis than the register's own generic 1840-1850 band; kept as a broad estimate around that point rather than a single sharp year. Girth and height: kanokaartutrecht states 'stamomtrek 550 cm' and a height of about 24 metres; sanity checked, both physically plausible for a mature plane. Distinctive feature per the same source: the gnarled, irregular shape of the lower trunk ('de grillige vorm van het onderste gedeelte van de stam'), otherwise typical peeling mottled bark and large fresh-green leaves. Species: Gewone Plataan, the same Dutch name used for the already-published London Planes on this map (utr_009/013/014/018); kept as London Plane (Platanus x acerifolia) for consistency, not Oriental Plane. Location: stands directly beside the Tolsteegbrug bridge at the water's edge, in Manenburg, one of the bastion parks along the old Stadsbuitengracht city-wall ring (the same Zocher-era park system as the already-published Zonnenburg and Wilhelminapark trees). Not a duplicate of utr_032 (The Black Walnut of the Tolsteegbrug), a different species about 94 metres away at the same bridge; two separate monumental trees flank the same crossing. Collectible point: yes, one identifiable trunk with a distinctive gnarled base, directly named by an independent route guide.

name: The Courthouse Planes of Hamburgerstraat

location.address: Hamburgerstraat, opposite no. 17, Utrecht (in front of the former Paleis van Justitie)

verified_sources: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen v2024 (Bomenstichting), entry nr 1678126, data/registers/netherlands-lrmb.json
access: Free, on a public square in front of the former Palace of Justice
transport: About a 10 minute walk from Utrecht Centraal station
verify_notes: Alive: register status 3, owner_category gemeente, visitable 'ja', visible 'ja', on a public square (plein). Two sources agree: the LRMB register (entry nr 1678126, 'Gewone plataan - Oude Rechtbank') gives a planted_band of 1850-1860 for the pair; oud-utrecht.nl's article 'De kippen van de concierge' (fetched directly, not from a search summary) independently dates the planting to around 1860, based on a circa-1875 photograph in which 'de boom in het midden van de foto (een van de platanen die er nu nog staat!) tien a vijftien jaar oud lijkt te zijn' (the tree in the middle of the photo, one of the planes still standing today, looks about ten to fifteen years old), i.e. planted around 1860-1865. The two sources converge without needing a bridge. History/story material: around 1860 four or five plane trees were planted in a newly laid-out square in front of the former Palace of Justice (built 1837 by Utrecht architect Christiaan Kramm on the remains of the Paulusabdij) specifically to screen the courthouse and a planned execution scaffold from the view of Hamburgerstraat's residents, who had objected to it; the scaffold itself was never used. Of that original planting, two trees survive today (this register entry, n_trees 2, a designed pair/courtyard planting rather than a chance duplicate; folding them into one entry per the register-twins rule). Two further planes were added in 1975 along the adjoining Korte Nieuwstraat and have grown nearly as large as their much older neighbours, per the same source, but those 1975 trees are not part of this monumental-register entry and are not included here. No girth or height figure found in either source for this specific pair; left unset rather than guessed. Species: register calls it Gewone Plataan; kept as London Plane (Platanus x acerifolia) for consistency with the other published Utrecht planes (utr_009/013/014/018/utr_036), not Oriental Plane. Collectible point: the pair stands together on one small square and reads as a single destination, the courtyard itself named by the source as the point of interest.
